Ty Masterson

Republican candidate for Governor / Lieutenant Governor, Kansas · Open seat

Kansas Senate President; state senator (R-Andover)

Ty Masterson is a Republican from Andover who has served in the Kansas Senate since 2009 and has been Senate President since 2021. Before that, he served in the Kansas House from 2005 to 2009. He won the Republican primary on August 4, 2026, and is running with Jeff Klemp for lieutenant governor in the November 3, 2026 race for the open seat of term-limited Gov. Laura Kelly.

Where Masterson stands

Property taxes
Calls property taxes his top issue. Proposes a 'Taxpayer Bill of Rights' that would cap property tax increases and local spending and would freeze or reduce property taxes for seniors on fixed incomes.
Property tax constitutional amendment
Says capping property taxes requires a constitutional amendment. In the 2026 session he sought an amendment to cap annual increases in assessed valuation.
Income and state taxes
Negotiated a 2024 plan with House Speaker Dan Hawkins and Gov. Kelly to cut property and income taxes over five years. Says the cuts give Kansans tax relief.
Education and literacy
Says Kansas has a literacy crisis and wants to 'bring Mississippi Miracle to Kansas' by focusing on early reading instruction.
School funding
Says the courts found in 2024 that Kansas funds schools adequately, and argues the issue is how the money is used rather than how much is spent.
Data centers
Says data center developers should pay their own electricity costs so nearby customers don't face higher rates. Supports protections for water, land and eminent domain, with local governments deciding whether projects go forward.
Medicaid expansion
Has opposed expanding Medicaid eligibility for lower-income Kansans.
Abortion
As Senate President, he has worked to expand state regulation of abortion.
Transgender policy
Says he advanced bills that ban gender-transition care for minors and bar transgender individuals from girls' and women's sports teams.
Marijuana
Opposes legalizing marijuana.

Background

  • Kansas House of Representatives, 2005–2009
  • Kansas Senate, 2009–present
  • Kansas Senate President, 2021–present
  • Director of GoCreate, a creative workspace at Wichita State University's Innovation Campus
  • Attended Kansas State University, left without a degree
  • Won Republican nomination for governor, August 4, 2026; running mate is Jeff Klemp
